Name: Sound Tweaker
Author: aedenthorn
Description:
This mod is a replacement for my Sound Effect Replacement mod that provides much more flexibility over sound effect and music replacement in Stardew Valley.

An example of a mod using this framework (actually the reason this framework came into existence) is [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/14631]Softer Snow Footstep Sound[/url].


[size=5][b]Basic Usage[/b][/size]

To use this mod, you will need to create a Content Patcher mod that targets this mod's dictionary.

[size=4][b]Cue Paths[/b][/size]

A simple content.json file is something like this:

[code]﻿{
    "Format": "1.23.0",
    "Changes": [
        {
            "Action": "EditData",
            "Target": "aedenthorn.SoundTweaker/dictionary",
            "Entries": {
                "snowyStep": {
                    "sounds": [
                        {
                            "cuePaths": [
                                "thudStep"
                            ]
                        }
                    ],
                }
            }
        }
    ]
}
[/code]
This simply replaces the [b]snowyStep[/b] sound with the [b]thudStep[/b] sound, preserving all parameters of the [b]thudStep[/b] sound.

The following page has the names of all the sound cues in the game:

[url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Audio#Track_list]https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Audio#Track_list[/url]


[size=4][b]File Paths[/b][/size]

Instead of [b]cuePaths[/b], you can direct the mod to play your own list of sound files using [b]filePaths[/b], e.g.:

[code]{
    "Format": "1.23.0",
    "Changes": [
        {
            "Action": "EditData",
            "Target": "aedenthorn.SoundTweaker/dictionary",
            "Entries": {
                "snowyStep": {
                    "sounds": [
                        {
                            "filePaths": [
                                "{{InternalAssetKey: sounds/Snowystep_Soft_01.wav}}",
                                "{{InternalAssetKey: sounds/Snowystep_Soft_02.wav}}",
                                "{{InternalAssetKey: sounds/Snowystep_Soft_03.wav}}"
                            ]
                        }
                    ],
                }
            }
        }
    ]
}
[/code]
These files have to be placed your Content Patcher mod's folder. The sound files above should be in a [b]sounds [/b]subfolder.

This method does not automatically preserve any sound parameters (in this case, the [b]snowyStep [/b]sound's random pitch). You must add your own sound parameters, as explained below.


[size=4][b]Sound Indexes[/b][/size]

Finally, you can target specific sound indexes in the sound bank using [b]soundIndexes[/b], e.g.:

[code]{
    "Format": "1.23.0",
    "Changes": [
        {
            "Action": "EditData",
            "Target": "aedenthorn.SoundTweaker/dictionary",
            "Entries": {
                "snowyStep": {
                    "sounds": [
                        {
                            "soundIndexes": [
                                86,
                                87,
                                88,
                                89,
                                90
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            }
        }
    ]
}
[/code]
This replaces the snowyStep sound with the four sounds associated with the [b]SpringBirds[/b] sound cue.

Use the following page to get the sound indexes for in-game sounds (use the ones under [b]decimal[/b]):

[url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Audio#Track_list]https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Audio#Track_list[/url]

Again, this method does not automatically preserve any sound parameters. See below to add your own parameters.


[size=4][b]Sound Disabling[/b][/size]

If you just want to silence a sound cue entirely, omit the [b]sounds[/b] key entirely. E.g.:

[code]﻿{
"Format": "1.23.0",
"Changes": [
  {
"Action": "EditData",
"Target": "aedenthorn.SoundTweaker/dictionary",
"Entries": {
"snowyStep": {
}
}
  }
]
}
[/code]
This will silence the [b]snowyStep[/b] sound cue entirely.


[size=5][b]Customization[/b][/size]

You can add the following keys to a dictionary entry to customize the sound cue:

[list]
[*][b]maxInstances[/b] - how many instances of this sound can be playing at once (default [b]1[/b])
[*][b]limitBehavior[/b] - what to do when more than the maxInstances try to play at once.  (default [b]ReplaceOldest[/b])
[/list]
Possible values for [b]limitBehavior[/b] are [b]ReplaceOldest[/b] and [b]FailToPlay[/b].

For each entry in the [b]sounds[/b] object of a dictionary entry, you can add the following keys to customize the tracks of individual sounds (one sound cue can contain multiple sounds, and one sound can contain multiple tracks):

[list]
[*][b]variationType[/b] - rule used to select a track to play. One of [b]Ordered[/b], [b]OrderedFromRandom[/b], [b]Random[/b], [b]RandomNoImmediateRepeats[/b], [b]Shuffle[/b].
[*][b]category[/b] - which category this sound belongs to. Affects sound volume. [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Audio#Category_list]See here[/url]﻿. One of [b]Music[/b], [b]Sound[/b], [b]Ambient[/b], [b]Footsteps[/b] (default is [b]Sound[/b]).
[b][/b][*][b]loop[/b] (true or [b]false[/b])
[*][b]reverb[/b] (true or [b]false[/b]) - I'm not sure this does anything at the moment.
[*][b]pitch[/b] - set a custom static pitch (1.0 is normal pitch, I think, or maybe 0)
[*][b]minPitch[/b] - set a custom random pitch minimum, must be used with [b]maxPitch[/b]
[*][b]maxPitch[/b] - set a custom random pitch maximum, must be used with [b]minPitch[/b]
[*][b]volume[/b] - set a custom static volume (1.0 is 100% volume). This is affected by the sound category.
[*][b]minVolume[/b] - set a custom random volume minimum, must be used with [b]maxVolume[/b]
[*][b]maxVolume[/b] - set a custom random volume maximum, must be used with [b]minVolume[/b]
[*][b]minFrequency[/b] - custom frequency variable, don't use unless you know what you're doing or like living dangerously
[*][b]maxFrequency[/b] - custom frequency variable
[*][b]minQ[/b] - custom frequency variable[b][/b]
[*][b]maxQ[/b] - custom frequency variable
[*][b]filterMode[/b] - one of [b]LowPass[/b], [b]BandPass[/b], [b]HighPass[/b]
[*][b]rpcCurves[/b] - list of rpc curve indexes. See below.
[/list]
An example content.json file that uses most of these parameters just to illustrate:

[code]{
 "Format": "1.23.0",
 "Changes": [
 {
"Action": "EditData",
"Target": "aedenthorn.SoundTweaker/dictionary",
"Entries": {
 "snowyStep": {
 "sounds": [
{
 "variationType": "RandomNoImmediateRepeats",
 "category": "Sound",
 "filePaths": [
 "aedenthorn.TestSound/guitar",
 "aedenthorn.TestSound/drum"
 ],
 "cuePaths": [
 "toyPiano",
 "flute"
 ],
 "soundIndexes": [
 257,
 258,
 259
 ],
 "loop": false,
 "reverb": false,
 "pitch": null,
 "minPitch": -1.0,
 "maxPitch": 1.0,
 "volume": null,
 "minVolume": 0.5,
 "maxVolume": 1.0,
 "minFrequency": 0.0,
 "maxFrequency": 1000.0,
 "minQ": 0.0,
 "maxQ": 500.0,
 "filterMode": "HighPass",
 "rpcCurves": [
 0
 ]
}
 ],
 "maxInstances": 1,
 "limitBehavior": 2
 }
}
 }
 ]
}[/code]
The above makes snowyStep sound like this:

[youtube]6Z2HJuj_Hvo[/youtube]


[size=5][b]RPC Curves
[/b][/size]
I don't even know what an RPC curve is, but I can tell you that Stardew Valley defines 11 of them. Here is the list for you to experiment:

[list]
[*]0 - 280,6,Pitch
[*]1 - 303,7,Volume
[*]2 - 335,8,FilterFrequency
[*]3 - 358,9,Pitch
[*]4 - 381,8,FilterFrequency
[*]5 - 404,8,FilterQFactor
[*]6 - 427,7,Volume
[*]7 - 477,8,FilterQFactor
[*]8 - 599,8,FilterFrequency
[*]9 - 658,8,Pitch
[*]10 - 708,7,Volume
[/list]
The first variable is called [b]Variable [/b]and the second variable is called [b]RpcCurve[/b]. The third variable is pretty obvious.


[size=5][b]Technical[/b][/size]

Requires [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2400/]SMAPI[/url].

Compatible with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/6338]Mod Updater[/url]﻿ for automatic updates.

Code is at [url=https://github.com/aedenthorn/StardewValleyMods]https://github.com/aedenthorn/StardewValleyMods[/url].

﻿﻿If you want to complain or ask for help or help me test my mods, you can visit [url=https://discord.gg/bs6zHuj]my Discord server﻿[/url].

A list of all my mods for Stardew Valley is available at [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/articles/895]https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/articles/895[/url].
